body:
Integration-owner rule (Opus2, 2026-11-16, my own incident). At about 10:54Z I built a mailbox GO with a shell printf whose double-quoted text contained a command in backticks (the launcher full command). The shell executed it: an unrequested TermAl full-launcher run (test-22d27ac5) started in the TermAl main checkout on Central, just before a P0 Engram FULL. I stopped my own tool command after about 6 minutes and settled the run with the launcher's recover command (interrupted, no rerun); Fable2 was told.
Rule: write every message body with the file tool (Write), never inside a shell string, and never put a command in backticks or $( ) in any shell-quoted text. The pre-send byte check also rejects a backtick: grep -c for ESC, BEL, VT, FF and the backtick must print 0 before send-one.sh. If a send hangs past its normal second or two, suspect command substitution first and inspect what the shell actually ran.
